_README: Pre-existing DB column/table references that do not resolve against database/schema/mysql-schema.sql. Read by scripts/check-db-column-references.mjs. SHRINK-ONLY: removing an entry is what a fix looks like; the gate FAILS if a listed entry no longer occurs, so a fix cannot land without updating this file. Adding an entry needs a reason in the commit message. Seeded 2026-07-30 when the gate was written.
_WHY: A documentation audit found docs citing a `group_bans` table that never existed. Chasing it down found the same defect three more times in the same service as a COLUMN mismatch on a table that does exist (writes to updated_at / moderated_at / action_taken on group_content_flags, whose real columns are resolved_at and moderation_action). Every write threw, and it went unnoticed for four months because each method wrapped its body in catch (\Throwable) and returned a plausible value. Provenance: commit de2e48396 (2026-03-20, 'add missing service methods') wrote 15 services against an imagined schema.
_FIXED_2026_07_30: All three `live-defect` entries are gone, fixed rather than re-baselined, and every one resolved as 'the code is wrong, the schema is right'. consent_types.tenant_id: the table is a PLATFORM-GLOBAL catalogue keyed by slug and FK'd from tenant_consent_overrides + consent_version_history, with per-tenant customisation done through the override table — so the admin CRUD dropped tenant_id and its three mutations now require a PLATFORM super admin, because a shared catalogue means every write is cross-tenant. challenge_claims: never created; the real claim ledger is user_challenge_progress.reward_claimed, so ChallengeService::claim was reimplemented on it to match GamificationV2Controller (the old version also never awarded anything, so creating the table would have made a visible failure silent). match_preference_categories: never created, and the canonical match_preferences.categories JSON column already persists the choices, so the vestigial side-table blocks were deleted. Two `verified` entries went with them (match_history.score / .distance) when the dead MatchingService::recordInteraction duplicate was removed. Regression cover: tests/Laravel/Feature/SchemaWriteRegressionTest.php FIX 7-9.
_FIXED_2026_08_28: Fifteen entries removed by DELETING the dead code rather than repairing it, because in every case a working implementation of the same job already exists elsewhere and the phantom one had no route and no caller. Deleted: HashtagService::syncTags (post_hashtags.tag — its unscoped ->delete() would have wiped a post's hashtag links before the insert threw); DeliverableService::create + ::addComment and DeliverableController::addComment (deliverables.project_id, deliverable_comments.body/.content — the service and the controller wrote DIFFERENT phantom column names for the same field, which is proof neither ever ran; the live path is AdminDeliverabilityController, which correctly writes deliverable_comments.comment_text); AdminListingsService::approve + ::reject (listings.approved_by/.approved_at — the live path is ListingModerationService); ExchangeService::decline (exchange_requests.provider_notes); GroupSSOService::findOrCreateSSOUser (users.auth_provider); LeaderboardSeasonService::endSeason (season_rankings.season_xp/.final_rank); SkillTaxonomyService::addSkill (user_skills.skill_id/.updated_at — the routed path is addUserSkill); AdminContentController::reports + ::approveContent + ::rejectContent (content_reports); AdminSettingsController::features + ::toggleFeature (tenant_features — real toggling is TenantFeatureConfig + tenants.features); CronJobService::run + ::getHistory (cron_job_runs — real monitoring is CronJobRunner); AuthService::refreshToken (api_tokens — real tokens are TokenService JWTs; the api_tokens entry below SURVIVES because AuthService::login/logout/validateToken/createApiToken still name that table).
_FIXED_2026_08_28_LIVE: comments.is_hidden was the LAST live-defect and is now FIXED, not deleted and not re-baselined. ContentModerationService::applyDecision() wrote comments.is_hidden in both the approve and reject branches; feed_posts has that column, comments does not — its only soft-hide column is deleted_at. Every comment decision therefore threw, the catch (\Throwable) swallowed it, and the queue row was still marked reviewed, so an admin rejecting a reported comment was told it was actioned while the comment stayed visible to every member. Reject now sets deleted_at = now() and approve clears it, which is the same test (`deleted_at IS NULL`) every read path already applies — CommentService, FeedService, FeedItemTables and PostAnalyticsController. It does conflate a member's own delete with a moderator's removal; the queue row records which, and separating them would need a migration. Regression cover: tests/Laravel/Feature/Moderation/CommentModerationAppliesDecisionTest.php, which reads the row back rather than mocking the database — the pre-existing unit tests mocked DB wholesale, which is why they never noticed.

_STATUS_MEANINGS.live-defect: Reachable in production and the write throws. Fix these.
_STATUS_MEANINGS.verified: Real mismatch, but the code path has no callers — dead. Delete or repair as a cleanup, not an incident.
_STATUS_MEANINGS.unreachable: Real mismatch; triaged 2026-07-30 and confirmed to have no callers or no route, so nothing hits it today. Still wrong, still worth removing.

api_tokens.note: The whole of App\Services\AuthService is dead: it is referenced only by its AppServiceProvider registration and its own tests, and real authentication is TokenService JWTs via AuthController. ::refreshToken was deleted on 2026-08-28; the remaining four references keep this entry alive. Retiring the class (and its container registration) is a separate decision, flagged for the owner.

_TRIAGE: Entries triaged 2026-07-30 against the LIVE dev database via information_schema, not just the committed dump: every one is ABSENT live as well, so there is ZERO dump drift here and every entry is a code defect. Positive controls (users.email, group_content_flags.resolved_at, match_history.match_score, post_hashtags.hashtag_id, user_skills.skill_name) all returned present, so the query discriminates. The live DB has 727 tables against the dump's 723, so minor drift exists — just not in any of these. Reachability was then established per entry; a first pass using bare method names was discarded because generic names like create() and run() matched hundreds of unrelated call sites. 🔴 LESSON FROM 2026-08-28: that second pass over-corrected. Searching for `->method(` misses a `private static` method called as `self::method(` and a static called as `Class::method(`, which is exactly how comments.is_hidden was mislabelled `unreachable` for four weeks while it was live. Search for the bare method name and READ the hits; do not trust an arrow-prefixed grep to prove a negative.
